headline: The sell-off stalled in the US but the leadership flipped — semis bid, crowded defensives dumped, oil back up 1.8%, and Brazil's real still the only thing accelerating.
summary: The liquidation did not continue; it rotated. SPX -0.2% to 7,399.8 after yesterday's -1.9%, NDX +0.1%, and the bounce came precisely where the damage was worst: SMH +0.6%, SOXX +0.8%, XBI +1.1%, high-beta/low-vol +1.0%, growth/value +0.4%. What paid for it was the crowded safe side — UNH -3.5%, HD -3.1%, XLV -1.0%, LLY -1.3%, XLU -0.8%, XLP -0.6%, SPLV -0.6%. VIX went nowhere (22.92, +0.0%) while VIX3M jumped 11.6% to 23.02: the curve got bid in the back, not the front, and SKEW is still at z=-2.0. This was de-grossing exhaustion, not a risk bid — RUT -1.7%, IPO -3.0%, OIH -3.8%, IAI -1.4%, VLUE -2.3%, JPM -1.3% all closed lower.

The epicentre moved again, this time to Europe and LatAm. Euro Stoxx -1.3%, DAX -1.2%, CAC -1.3%, FTSE -1.3%, ASX -1.8% — the first synchronised European down day of this drawdown, with EURUSD at 1.0996 (0th percentile of the year, -1.9% on the month) against a DXY at 103.62 and the 100th percentile; the dollar composite is -48. Asia's US-listed proxies finally marked the damage: EWT -1.8% (Taiwan z=-2.55, TAIEX -14.9% on the month), KOSPI -2.6% and 24.5% below its 200-day, Nikkei -1.3% at z=-2.10. And the single most extreme print on the board got more extreme: USDBRL +2.0% to 5.7755, +13.3% on the month, z=3.77 with acceleration +2.77 for a third consecutive day. EWZ's +1.2% today is noise against -25.2% on the month (z=-3.25); Bovespa acceleration is -3.47. Argentina -4.3% and at the 0th percentile. This is still dispersion, not a blanket EM unwind — India and Mexico are going the other way.

The rates picture is unchanged in level and worse in mix. 10-year 5.15%, real 10-year 2.91% (+50bp in three months, 29.5% above its 200-day), 2-year 4.88% after +37bp in a week, MOVE 101.28 and +17.8% on the week. Against that, 10-year breakevens sit at 2.20% (6th percentile) and 5-year at 2.25% while core CPI is turning up at z=0.93 and headline CPI at z=0.65. That gap is the trade: today crude bounced — WTI +1.8% to 87.29, Brent +1.7% to 94.00 and +2.7% on the week after a -14.4% month (z=-1.53) — XOP +0.7% and +3.2% on the week with relative strength turning up. If oil has put in a low with inflation compensation at the 6th percentile, the disinflation half of the real-rate shock reverses and long duration gets hurt again, not rescued. The one genuine easing impulse is mortgages: 30-year at 7.11%, -29bp on the month with acceleration z=-2.36, which is why ITB is +7.4% and XHB +5.6% on the month.

What is still holding is credit and breadth, and that remains the case against wholesale de-risking. HY OAS 3.23 (+3bp), IG 0.89, BKLN at the 95th percentile, HYG/IEF turning up. Equal-weight/cap-weight is z=2.62 with acceleration 1.80; transports/S&P +2.3% today at z=2.41 with UPS +16.4% and FDX +11.4% on the month. The macro underneath is fine: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%). The quiet deterioration is in quality and in the growth proxies: CCC spreads 13.16, +34bp on the month at the 92nd percentile while HY sits still; IG and BBB spread z-scores of 0.78 and 0.89; bank reserves -2.3% on the month and NFCI tightening at z=0.31. Copper -8.4% on the month, COPX -17.8%, FCX -20.1%, XME -10.2%, CAT -21.5% at z=-2.46 — the real economy cyclicals are not confirming the equity stabilisation.

good.text: Credit still refuses to participate in the equity drawdown: HY OAS 3.23 (+3bp on the day, -2bp on the month), IG 0.89, leveraged loans at the 95th percentile and HYG/IEF turning up. No funding stress yet.

Breadth is the strongest signal on the board: equal-weight/cap-weight z=2.62 with acceleration 1.80, SPW at the 88th percentile, transports/S&P +2.3% today at z=2.41, UPS +16.4% and FDX +11.4% on the month.
Vol did not follow through. VIX flat at 22.92 after +18% yesterday, SKEW -13.2% on the month at z=-2.0 and acceleration -2.63 — tail protection is cheap, nobody is panicking, only de-grossing.

Crude found a bid after a -14% month: WTI +1.8% to 87.29, Brent +1.7% to 94.00 and +2.7% on the week, XOP +3.2% on the week with relative strength turning up. That rebuilds inflation compensation from a 6th-percentile base.

Mortgage rates are easing fastest of anything in the rates complex — 7.11%, -29bp on the month, acceleration z=-2.36 — and housing equities have responded: ITB +7.4%, XHB +5.6% on the month, XHB/SPY z=1.68.
Labour and demand data are not rolling over: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), retail sales +4.7% YTD. Growth pulse composite +2.

bad.text: Brazil is a live accident: USDBRL +2.0% to 5.7755, +13.3% on the month, z=3.77 with acceleration +2.77 — third straight day of acceleration. Bovespa acceleration -3.47, EWZ -25.2% on the month. Argentina -4.3% today, -19.8% on the month at the 0th percentile.

The dollar is squeezing the world: DXY 103.62 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD 1.0996 at the 0th, USDCHF and USDCAD both at the 100th, EM FX basket -1.4% on the month and AUD/JPY rolling over at z=-0.86.

The real-rate engine is still running: 10-year TIPS yield 2.91% (+50bp in three months, 29.5% above its 200-day), 2-year 4.88% after +37bp in a week, MOVE 101.28 and +33.9% in three months — with 10-year breakevens at the 6th percentile. Tight policy into softening nominal growth.

Europe joined the downside for the first time: Euro Stoxx -1.3%, DAX -1.2%, CAC -1.3%, FTSE -1.3%, with the ETF versions (EWG -1.4%, EWI -1.4%, EWP -1.3%) marking it. The one regional offset to US weakness is thinning.

Quality is quietly degrading inside credit: CCC spreads 13.16, +34bp on the month at the 92nd percentile while HY sits flat; IG and BBB spread z-scores of 0.78 and 0.89; bank reserves -2.3% on the month and NFCI tightening at z=0.31.
The cyclical complex is not confirming the equity bounce: copper -8.4% on the month, COPX -17.8%, FCX -20.1%, XME -10.2% at the 8th percentile, CAT -21.5% at z=-2.46 and 28.7% below its 200-day.

trades.name: Short long duration into sticky core inflation
trades.line: Short TLT: 2.91% real 10y, breakevens at 6th pctile, core CPI up
trades.expr: Short TLT outright (79.31), or buy the 3-month 78/73 put spread. Cheaper carry version: short IEF.
trades.thesis: The market has priced the disinflation half of the story to an extreme — 10y breakevens 2.20% at the 6th percentile, 5y 2.25% — while core CPI is turning up at z=0.93 and crude just bounced 1.8%. Real yields at 2.91% are the pain, and if inflation compensation re-builds, nominal yields go higher, not lower. TLT is already in a downtrend at the 23rd percentile with MOVE +17.8% on the week.
trades.trigger: 10y 5.15% (+5bp), 2y +37bp in a week, 30y 5.47%, MOVE 101.28; WTI +1.8% and Brent +2.7% on the week off a -14% month, with 10y breakevens at 2.20%.
trades.stop: TLT back above 83 — i.e. a genuine growth scare (claims above 230k, payroll break) that drags real yields down with breakevens.

trades.name: Long energy producers vs crowded staples
trades.line: Long XOP / short XLP: oil turning, defensives at 97th pctile
trades.expr: Long XOP, short an equal dollar of XLP. Overlay: long Jan XOP 190 calls funded by XLP calls if you want convexity.
trades.thesis: Crude washed out (WTI z=-1.43, Brent z=-1.53, gasoline -21.5% on the month) and is now bid; XOP relative strength has turned up with +3.2% on the week. XLP is the most crowded defensive on the board — 97th percentile, 9.4% above its 200-day, z=1.19 — and it cracked today while semis rallied. You get an inflation-rebuild hedge and a positioning unwind in one trade.
trades.trigger: WTI +1.8% to 87.29 and Brent +1.7% to 94.00 with XLE +2.8% on the week, against XLP -0.6% today and -1.1%... breakevens at the 6th percentile leave plenty of room to re-price.
trades.stop: WTI back under 82 (new low versus the -13.9% monthly move) or the pair down 5%.

trades.name: Short Brazil, long Mexico
trades.line: Short EWZ / long EWW: USDBRL z=3.77 and still accelerating
trades.expr: Short EWZ, long an equal dollar of EWW. Size for 2x realised vol of a normal LatAm pair.
trades.thesis: The most extreme reading on the entire board is BRL and it is re-accelerating, not mean-reverting: USDBRL +2.0% today, +13.3% on the month, z=3.77, acceleration +2.77 for a third straight session. Equity is a lagging mirror of the currency — EWZ -25.2% on the month, Bovespa acceleration -3.47 — so today's +1.2% EWZ bounce is a gift. Mexico is the other side of the same regional book: IPC +6.6% on the month, USDMXN flat with acceleration -1.79, EWW +2.3% on the month and turning up.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +2.0% while EWZ rallied 1.2% — the currency and the equity disagreed today; Bovespa z=-3.26.
trades.stop: USDBRL back below 5.45, or the pair down 6%.

trades.name: Transports over the rest of industrials
trades.line: Long IYT / short XLI: IYT/SPY z=2.41, XLI rs -6.2% on 3m
trades.expr: Long IYT, short an equal dollar of XLI. Single-name expression: long UPS and FDX against CAT.
trades.thesis: Transports are the cleanest breadth signal in the tape and they are being driven by falling fuel costs and firm volumes: IYT/SPY +8.2% on the month at z=2.41 with acceleration 1.80, DJT +3.6% on the month, UPS +16.4% (z=2.08), FDX +11.4%. The rest of industrials is the AI/capex and machinery complex that is breaking — XLI -1.2% on the month, relative strength -6.2% over three months, CAT -21.5% at z=-2.46.
trades.trigger: IYT/SPY +2.3% today on a down tape; gasoline -21.5% on the month and diesel-sensitive XTN +5.1%, versus XLI rolling over.
trades.stop: Pair down 4%, or IYT/SPY closing back below its 200-day (currently 1.1% above).

trades.name: Short the AI power-capex complex, long software
trades.line: Short GEV+GRID / long IGV: capex unwind, software rs turning up
trades.expr: Short GEV and GRID equally, long an equal total dollar of IGV. Alternative short leg: ETN or VST.
trades.thesis: The electricity-for-AI trade is unwinding faster than the AI trade itself: GEV -15.5% on the month (z=-1.62, 18.1% below its 200-day), ETN -12.8% (z=-1.88), VST -14.2%, GRID -8.1% with relative strength -11.7% over three months, NLR -9.6% and uranium -14.4%. Software is the opposite — IGV/SMH z=1.46, +9.9% on the month, +18.7% on three months, and IGV relative strength turning up. Capex deflation is bad for the picks-and-shovels, neutral-to-good for the opex side.
trades.trigger: GEV +1.9% and ETN +1.0% today on a dead-cat semis bounce, with both still in rolling-over trends 14-18% below their 200-days; IGV/SMH acceleration +0.85.
trades.stop: GEV reclaims its 200-day, or the pair down 7%.

trades.name: Long India against the EM index
trades.line: Long INDA / short EEM: Sensex z=2.45, INR the only EM FX firming
trades.expr: Long INDA, short an equal dollar of EEM.
trades.thesis: EM is dispersion, not a single trade, and India is on the right side of it. Sensex +10.4% on the month at z=2.45 with acceleration 1.74, INDA +8.6% at z=1.91 with relative strength +12.3%, and USDINR -0.8% today, -1.1% on the month at z=-1.28 — the only major EM currency improving while the EM basket is -1.4% and USDBRL is at z=3.77. EEM is dragged by Korea, Taiwan and Brazil, all of which are still breaking.
trades.trigger: India up 0.5% while Taiwan -2.3%, KOSPI -2.6%, HSI -1.0% and EEM -0.7%; EEM/SPY z=-0.82 at the 4th percentile of the year.
trades.stop: USDINR back above 95, or the pair down 4%.
